transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brings me in is my eating. I have these times where I just eat way too much, and... after I do it, I just sit there looking at all the empty containers, and I feel completely disgusted with myself. I've always tried to be a steady, in-control man, you know? And when this happens, it just feels like I'm not that man at all. It's really getting to me, so I figured it was time to talk to somebody.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever do anything to try to prevent weight gain, such as vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do anything like that. I just... sit there and feel terrible about it. I don't throw up or take pills or go run miles or anything. I'm on the road a lot for work, driving my truck, so I don't really have the time or energy for heavy exercise anyway. But no, I don't try to get rid of the food once I've eaten it. I just live with it.

latest_inference.note: The patient explicitly denied compensatory behaviors (vomiting, laxatives, excessive exercise), which rules out F50.2 (Bulimia Nervosa) and F50.9 (Eating disorder, unspecified). The clinical presentation is consistent with Binge Eating Disorder.
